newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INRO hikes rubber buffer stock reference price.
newsitem.headline: INRO hikes rubber buffer stock reference price.

text.p: The International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) said on Friday it had raised its buffer stock reference price by four percent to reflect increase in world rubber prices.

The reference price has been raised to 214.95 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg from 206.68 cents, INRO said in a statement issued at the end of its first council meeting under the International Natural Rubber Agreement 3 (INRA 3).
"The old reference price is not valid any more as the market price of rubber has been higher throughout the year," INRO's buffer stock manager James Hegarty told Reuters after the council meeting.
The reference price is basically a neutral level where INRO's buffer stock manager does not intervene to buy or sell rubber in the market.
The price is calculated as a weighted average of the Singapore and Malaysian currencies.
